options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every norm-bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Identify and verify a precise monotone sequential completeness theorem whose hypotheses match the definition in the problem. If it applies, conclude that the required absence of a least upper bound is impossible, independently of the quasitrace increments.

options.approach: Attempt to construct the supremum directly from spectral projections and the right-annihilator property. Track carefully whether the construction gives a least upper bound in the full self-adjoint order rather than only within an abelian subalgebra.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every norm-bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether finite-factor projection dimension permits reduction of an arbitrary increasing sequence to compatible bounded operators on increasing projections. Establishing that these pieces glue to their least upper bound would prove the required completeness.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace and a sequence satisfying all the problem's conditions with increment exactly one half.
options.approach: Analyze the simultaneous endpoint identities: every nonempty finite sum of increments must have quasitrace one half. Seek an explicit construction realizing these identities, checking faithfulness and the absence of a least upper bound separately.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace and a sequence satisfying all the problem's conditions with increment exactly one half.
options.approach: Investigate whether examples with increments approaching one half can be assembled into a quasitracial ultraproduct. Verify that the quotient remains a finite AW*-factor and use a diagonal argument to test whether the limiting sequence lacks a least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace and a sequence satisfying all the problem's conditions with increment exactly one half.
options.approach: Starting from an endpoint witness, prove that scalar rescaling preserves every required condition. Combined with the two-increment upper bound, this would establish that the exact set is the interval from zero, excluded, to one half, included.

options.approach: Audit the claimed quasitracial completeness theorem, distinguishing completeness of the entire algebra from completeness of uniformly norm-bounded sets. Locate exactly which property is required to turn a Cauchy increasing sequence into its supremum.
